candidates.tagline: 6 years. 38 patents. 5,126 prototypes. Dyson made a $499 toothbrush that leaks.
candidates.story: Dyson's CameraJet launched September 1, 2026 — a $499 electric toothbrush with a built-in camera and AI that streams a live view of your teeth to your phone; within two weeks, units started failing due to water seeping into battery compartments, and the product was pulled from multiple retailers while Dyson scrambled to find the fault in a device designed for daily use inside a human mouth.
candidates.why_funny: Dyson spent six years and 38 patents engineering a toothbrush complex enough to watch your own teeth, and its single biggest flaw is that water gets in — which is the one thing a toothbrush is guaranteed to encounter every time.
candidates.alt: A person holds the pink and white Dyson CameraJet electric toothbrush in their mouth while watching their smartphone, which displays a live camera view of the inside of their mouth via the CameraJet's built-in lens

candidates.tagline: Apple's new $299 smart home hub launches Nov 13 — shipping with six-month-old software, no YouTube, and banned from Europe
candidates.story: Apple's HomeView smart home display launches November 13, 2026 for $299, but pre-launch code analysis revealed it ships with HomeView OS 26.5 — software already six months out of date — while also lacking YouTube, Netflix, and most third-party apps at launch, and being entirely unavailable in the EU because its flagship Siri AI feature is blocked there by regulators.
candidates.why_funny: Apple spent years positioning its AI-first smart home hub as the definitive answer to Amazon Echo, then shipped it running half-year-old firmware, without the apps people actually watch, and unable to legally sell it in one of the world's biggest consumer markets.
candidates.alt: Apple HomeView smart home display, a compact rounded-square device with a 7-inch screen showing the Siri AI interface, sitting on a mesh speaker base, with an iPhone beside it displaying Siri AI conversation results
